# Employment Contract Templates — Full Documentation Overview

## Overview

This skill provides templates and patterns for creating legally sound employment documentation, including **contracts, offer letters, and HR policies**. It includes legal best practices and three complete templates.

> **⚠️ DISCLAIMER:** These templates are for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice. Consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.

---

## When to Use This Skill

- Drafting employment contracts
- Creating offer letters
- Writing employee handbooks
- Developing HR policies
- Standardizing employment documentation
- Onboarding documentation

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. Employment Document Types

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies & procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

### 2. Key Legal Considerations

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

---

## Template 1: Offer Letter

A pre-hire document extending a formal job offer, including:

**Key Sections:**
- **Header** — Company letterhead, date, candidate contact info
- **Position Details** — Title, department, reporting structure, location, start date, employment type (Full-Time/Part-Time, Exempt/Non-Exempt)
- **Compensation** — Base salary, bonus eligibility, equity grants
- **Benefits** — Health insurance, 401(k) match, PTO, holidays
- **Contingencies** — Background check, right-to-work verification, required signed documents (NDA, Non-Compete, IP Assignment)
- **At-Will Employment Statement** — Clarifies the letter is not a contract for a specific period
- **Acceptance Section** — Signature lines for candidate, printed name, date, anticipated start date, and an offer **expiration deadline**

---

## Template 2: Employment Agreement (Contract Position)

A formal employment agreement for contract positions, organized into 9 main sections plus exhibits:

**Section Highlights:**

1. **Employment** — Position, duties, best-efforts expectation, location/remote arrangements
2. **Term** — Start date; choose between **At-Will** language or **Fixed Term** language depending on your structure
3. **Compensation** — Base salary, discretionary bonus, equity (separate Stock Option Agreement), benefits plan participation, business expense reimbursement
4. **Confidentiality** — Defines Confidential Information, non-disclosure obligations (both during and after employment), return-of-materials requirement, survival terms (indefinite for trade secrets; typically 3 years otherwise)
5. **Intellectual Property** — Company ownership of Work Product, full assignment of rights, assistance clause, and **Exhibit A** for listing prior inventions
6. **Non-Competition & Non-Solicitation** — 12-month restrictions on competing businesses, customer solicitation, and employee recruitment. *(Note: enforceability varies by jurisdiction — consult local counsel)*
7. **Termination** — Cause definitions (material breach, felony conviction, fraud/misconduct, failure to perform after cure period), notice periods, severance contingent on release agreement, and post-termination effects (earned compensation paid, unvested equity forfeited, specified sections survive)
8. **General Provisions** — Entire agreement, amendments by written consent only, governing law, dispute resolution/arbitration, severability, notices, assignment restrictions, waiver
9. **Acknowledgments** — Employee confirms reading, understanding, opportunity for counsel, and voluntary agreement

**Closing/Signature Block:** Signature lines for both the Company (authorized signatory) and Employee, plus **Exhibit A: Prior Inventions** form.

---

## Template 3: Employee Handbook Policy Section

An onboarding policy reference covering:

- **Equal Employment Opportunity** — Non-discrimination statement applicable to all employment practices
- **Anti-Harassment Policy** — Prohibited conduct examples (sexual advances, offensive comments, physical/visual conduct, threatening behavior), formal reporting procedure (manager/HR/leadership, written or verbal, anonymous hotline), and investigation/retaliation protections
- **Work Hours & Attendance** — Standard hours, core availability hours, flexible/remote work policies, absence notification and disciplinary thresholds
- **Paid Time Off (PTO)** — Accrual table by years of service (15 days for 0–2 yrs; 20 days for 3–5 yrs; 25 days for 6+ yrs), accrual mechanics, maximum accrual caps, advance notice requirements, blackout periods
- **Sick Leave** — Allotted days, permitted uses (personal illness or family care), doctor's note requirements beyond 3 days
- **Holidays** — Standard paid holiday list including a floating holiday
- **Code of Conduct** — Integrity, respect, confidentiality, conflict-of-interest avoidance, legal compliance, reporting violations
- **Technology & Communication** — Acceptable use (business purpose with limited personal use), monitoring notice with no expectation of privacy, security requirements (strong passwords, 2FA, incident reporting, device locking)
- **Social Media Policy** — Personal use disclaimers, no confidential info sharing; company account posting restricted to authorized personnel with brand guidelines
- **Acknowledgment Section** — Employee signs confirming responsibility to read the handbook, understanding that it does not create a contract, policies may change, and employment remains at-will where applicable

---

## Best Practices

### ✅ Do's
- **Consult legal counsel** — Employment law varies by jurisdiction
- **Keep copies signed** — Document all agreements
- **Update regularly** — Laws and policies change
- **Be clear and specific** — Avoid ambiguity
- **Train managers** — On policies and procedures

### ❌ Don'ts
- **Don't use generic templates** — Customize for your jurisdiction
- **Don't make promises** — That could create implied contracts
- **Don't discriminate** — In language or application
- **Don't forget at-will language** — Where applicable
- **Don't skip review** — Have legal counsel review all documents

---

## External Resources

- [SHRM Employment Templates](https://www.shrm.org/) — Society for Human Resource Management
- [Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/) — Federal labor guidelines
- [EEOC Guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/) — Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
- State-specific labor departments — For jurisdiction-specific requirements

---

## Key Takeaways for Use

1. **Choose the right template** — Offer letter for pre-hire; employment agreement for formal contract positions; handbook sections for onboarding/policies.
2. **Customize the bracketed placeholders** `[LIKE THIS]` for every document — no field should remain blank.
3. **Make the at-will vs. fixed-term decision** up front, as it affects the term, termination, and severance language throughout the agreement.
4. **Include all contingencies** (background check, work authorization, signed ancillary agreements) in offer letters.
5. **Pair the employment agreement with ancillary documents** — NDA, non-compete, IP assignment — referenced in the contingencies section.
6. **Always add the disclaimer** that templates are informational only and require review by qualified legal counsel.
